binary_provenance.density7-*, arm3-*: 33fda161 (secondary follower records and retries catch-up errors instead of exiting)

mainnet_targets.arm1_density: Bytes per block: September 2026 Mainnet mean 74,874 B vs this Testnet range's 23,159 B = 3.23x. Measured effective byte multipliers (combined): x4 -> 2.37, x7 -> 3.31; canonical-only: x4 -> 2.88, x7 -> 4.29. Transparent inputs plus outputs per block: September 2026 Mainnet 36.2 vs Testnet 51.8 = 0.70x, so wallet rows are already Mainnet-dense or denser at x1.
mainnet_targets.arm2_density: Densest 1000-block Testnet window 4617272..4618271: 197.7 MB raw, 480.3k transparent inputs plus outputs. Densest 2026 Mainnet day by bytes (2026-09-03): 231.6 MB per 1000 blocks (window is 0.85x); densest by transparent rows (2026-09-23): 131.7k per 1000 blocks (window is 3.6x). The newest 1000 blocks at T (the spec's Arm 2 window) are sparse: 8.47 MB raw.
mainnet_targets.post_nu7_tip: Mainnet week after NU7 (2026-11-07..13, 25 s blocks): 26,949 B per block, 9.4 transparent inputs plus outputs per block (1.16x and 0.18x this Testnet range).

observations: The 2x p99 miss comes from the wallet planner on transparent-dense blocks: 448 Arm 1 blocks with >= 1000 transparent inputs plus outputs cost 0.114 ms of planning per input or output with 6.3 point reads each; 53 combined commits exceeded 1 s (max 4.75 s); the canonical-only maximum was 0.41 s. On blocks with <= 3 transparent inputs plus outputs the combined p99 is 39.5 ms against 26.2 ms (1.51x). Mainnet had 0.78% of September 2026 blocks with >= 300 transparent inputs and 0.42% with >= 300 outputs.

Arm 3 stops are memtable-limit stops (max_write_buffer_number 2, atomic_flush) entered by every family together, canonical families and the default family included. With pressure on the wallet mirror families only (21 lanes, 8.66x), canonical families recorded 13 memtable-limit stop entries and the commit thread waited 0.44 s in total: canonical commits do stall on wallet-family write load under the production options, before any per-family tuning.

Out-of-process canonical secondary catch-up hit transient errors under high write volume: 'canonical replay at height N is absent' and 'No such file or directory' for an SST the primary had compacted away. One error ended the first density x7 canonical-only attempt (evidence in failed-runs/); after the follower was changed to record and retry, Arm 3 runs logged 4, 4, 4, and 2 errors, each recovered on a later poll, and the final fences matched. The canonical secondary has no transient-error retry; the materialized-view secondary does (is_transient_secondary_missing_sst).

Writer VmHWM grows with the replacement batch: dense window x1 645 MB batch -> 2.83 GiB, x2 1.29 GB -> 6.07 GiB, x4 2.58 GB -> 10.68 GiB. VmHWM also rose across successive replacements in one process (x2: 5.15 to 6.07 GiB).

Wallet plan logical bytes (batch plus overlay) for the dense window: 540 MB at x1 (above the projector's 512 MiB default follow ceiling, within the 1 GiB planner maximum), 1.08 GB at x2 and 2.16 GB at x4 (above the 1 GiB maximum; the mirror lanes are charged outside the planner, so the real planner would have refused these).

ingest.follow.max_replacement_bytes (2 GiB) does not bound the combined batch: the measured batch-to-held ratio on the dense window is 2.69, so the 2.5 GiB batch ceiling corresponds to about 1.0 GB of ingest-held bytes.
limits: Testnet only. No Mainnet store or node on the host; Mainnet-like rows are mirror lanes in separate mirror_* families, and Mainnet density comes from Blockchair third-party aggregates, not a node.

Mirror lanes scale every block uniformly (clamped so no scaled block exceeds 2,000,000 bytes), so Testnet's transparent stress blocks are scaled too; mirror point reads mostly miss; per-commit control, epoch, and event records and canonical prepare CPU are not scaled; Arm 2 lanes are not clamped per block.

Tip cadence means back-to-back synced commits, not 25 s spacing. Arm 3's per-hour figure is per replayed chain hour (347 chain hours replayed in about 33 minutes); per wall hour the same runs are 1.5 to 218 s.
Arm 2 re-commits identical blocks on the replacement parent; no real fork with different transactions was replayed.

Each arm ran once (Arm 1 combined also repeated over 48,149 blocks). The host was shared: other work raised the load average to about 10 and moved free disk between 28 and 76 GB during the run, so latencies may include interference.
The secondary runs out of process with a 1 s poll in replay arms (catch-up once per replacement in Arm 2), not after every block. In-process snapshot serving is not measured here.
The x8 ingest-cap probe was skipped for disk; its batch (about 5.78 GB) is a linear extrapolation.
RocksDB options are the production ones; no per-family tuning was tried. Bulk construction, the stage join, crash and truncation paths, and planner read batching (multi_get) were not tested.
